manifests.title: Numerator-denominator role map
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: The denominator creates three continuity intervals.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify rational functions and determine all excluded inputs from the original denominator before simplifying.

manifests.title: Domain intervals
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for rational functions and their domains.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify rational functions and determine all excluded inputs from the original denominator before simplifying.

manifests.title: No-real-zero denominator
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why simplifying before recording the original exclusions leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify rational functions and determine all excluded inputs from the original denominator before simplifying.

manifests.title: Cancellation with domain memory
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: The original denominator excludes 3.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify removable discontinuities caused by common factors and distinguish formula equivalence from function equality.

manifests.title: Hole coordinate construction
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for equivalent formulas, different functions, and holes.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify removable discontinuities caused by common factors and distinguish formula equivalence from function equality.

manifests.title: Equal expressions versus functions
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why filling the hole because the simplified formula has a value there leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify removable discontinuities caused by common factors and distinguish formula equivalence from function equality.

manifests.title: One-sided arrows
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: The first-power denominator changes sign.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine vertical asymptotes and describe one-sided behavior from factor signs and multiplicity.

manifests.title: Multiplicity comparison
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for vertical asymptotes and local behavior.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine vertical asymptotes and describe one-sided behavior from factor signs and multiplicity.

manifests.title: Local sign ledger
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why treating an asymptote as a function point or assuming both sides behave alike leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine vertical asymptotes and describe one-sided behavior from factor signs and multiplicity.

manifests.title: Degree comparison chart
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: Equal degrees use leading coefficient ratio.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine horizontal asymptotes from degree comparison and interpret them as long-run output behavior.

manifests.title: Leading-term quotient
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for horizontal asymptotes and end behavior.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine horizontal asymptotes from degree comparison and interpret them as long-run output behavior.

manifests.title: Asymptote crossing
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why applying the equal-degree ratio to unequal degrees leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine horizontal asymptotes from degree comparison and interpret them as long-run output behavior.

manifests.title: Division decomposition
manifests.description: Follow the foundation example from its given information to the conclusion. The labels identify the mathematical feature that makes the result valid: The remainder measures the gap.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use polynomial division to determine nonhorizontal asymptotes and describe the shrinking remainder term.

manifests.title: Slant approach
manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for slant and polynomial asymptotes.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use polynomial division to determine nonhorizontal asymptotes and describe the shrinking remainder term.

manifests.title: Polynomial asymptote
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why claiming the rational function equals the quotient everywhere leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use polynomial division to determine nonhorizontal asymptotes and describe the shrinking remainder term.

manifests.learnerOutcome: Find rational intercepts and determine positive and negative intervals using factored sign structure.

manifests.description: Read the numbered reasoning path in order. Each stage preserves the quantities, restrictions, or structural conditions needed for intercepts and sign charts.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Find rational intercepts and determine positive and negative intervals using factored sign structure.

manifests.title: Multiplicity at rational zero
manifests.description: Compare the valid path with the tempting shortcut. The figure shows why counting a cancelled numerator zero as an intercept leads to a false conclusion.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Find rational intercepts and determine positive and negative intervals using factored sign structure.

manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct a complete rational graph using domain, discontinuities, asymptotes, intercepts, signs, and selected values.
